elements.description: When a person decides: the conditions that pause a run, who reviews, what they see, what they may do and why.

properties.name: value
properties.description: The gate's config. Changed by the user unless a tc-value-change listener calls preventDefault()

properties.name: conditions
properties.default: [ { id: "low-confidence", label: "Confidence is low", description: "The agent rates its own answer under the threshold" }, { id: "no-source", label: "A claim has no source", description: "Something in the output isn't backed by a retrieved source" }, { id: "irreversible", label: "The next action can't be undone", description: "Sending, paying, deleting or publishing" }, { id: "personal-data", label: "It touches personal data", description: "Names, contact details or records about a person" }, { id: "new-version", label: "The playbook just changed", description: "The first ten runs after a new version" }, ]
properties.description: The conditions that can pause a run, each shown as a switch

properties.name: reviewers
properties.default: [ { id: "owner", label: "Whoever started the run" }, { id: "lead", label: "A team lead" }, { id: "on-call", label: "The on-call reviewer" }, { id: "named", label: "A named approver" }, ]
properties.description: Who can review, offered in the Reviewer select

properties.name: views
properties.default: [ { id: "output", label: "Output", phrase: "the output", description: "The result only, as it would go out" }, { id: "evidence", label: "With evidence", phrase: "the output with its evidence", description: "The result, the sources behind it and the agent's confidence" }, { id: "trace", label: "Full trace", phrase: "the full trace", description: "Every step, tool call and source of the run" }, ]
properties.description: What a reviewer can be shown, offered as a segmented control – two to four work best

properties.name: actions
properties.default: [ { id: "approve", label: "Approve", description: "The run carries on as it is" }, { id: "edit", label: "Edit and approve", description: "Change the output, then carry on" }, { id: "send-back", label: "Send back", description: "The agent tries again with the reviewer's note" }, { id: "escalate", label: "Escalate", description: "Hand the decision to someone more senior" }, { id: "reject", label: "Reject", description: "The run stops here" }, ]
properties.description: The actions a reviewer may be allowed, shown as checkboxes

properties.name: heading
properties.description: Names the group, shown at the top

properties.name: description
properties.description: A quieter line under the heading, e.g. which step the gate guards

properties.name: placeholder
properties.default: "Why a person decides here – the reviewer reads this first"

properties.name: flat
properties.description: Drops the tray and the card, for a gate inside another card

properties.name: name
properties.description: Submitted with the form: the config as JSON

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Turns every control off and leaves the config out of the form; a disabled fieldset does the same

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-value-change
events.description: The config changed ({ value: GateConfigValue }); cancelable – prevent it to control `value`

functions.name: describeGate
functions.signature: describeGate(value: GateConfigValue, o: { conditions?: GateCondition[]; reviewers?: GateReviewer[]; views?: GateView[]; actions?: GateActionOption[] }): string
functions.description:
The gate in plain words: "Pauses when confidence is low or a claim has no source, for a team lead to review the
output with its evidence. They may approve, send back or reject."

props.name: title
props.description: Shown at the top; names the group

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The config to start with when uncontrolled

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the whole config after every change

changelog: **Trust & calibration**, from THEMIS and built domain-neutral: - claims and their reliability: `tc-claim-answer`, `tc-verification-queue`, `tc-reflection-gate`, `tc-reliance-gauge`, `tc-disagreement-banner`, `tc-synthesis-notes`; - where outputs came from: `tc-lineage-graph`, `tc-validity-badge`, `tc-provenance-summary`, `tc-correction-propagation`, `tc-attestation-check`, `tc-run-manifest`; - policy and control: `tc-policy-simulator`, `tc-gate-config`, `tc-coverage-matrix`, `tc-kill-switch`, `tc-playbook-canvas`.

features.name: light-dark()
features.why: Every colour token is a light / dark pair; without it no colour token resolves.

features.name: Form association (ElementInternals)
features.why: The element's value is submitted with its form, and it takes part in form validation and reset.

features.name: color-mix()
features.why: Tints and washes mixed from the tokens.

features.name: Container size queries
features.why: Components adapt to the width they're given, not the window's.

features.name: :is() and :where()
features.why: Every rule is keyed on :where() so the page can override it.

features.name: field-sizing
features.without: Text fields grow with their text. Without it they keep their minimum height and scroll.

features.name: scrollbar-width
features.without: Scrollbars keep the browser's default width.

features.name: @property
features.without: The registered custom properties don't interpolate, so the transitions and spins they drive jump to their end state.

features.name: adoptedStyleSheets
features.without: Each element type's CSS goes into one <style> element in <head> instead – it looks and works the same.

features.name: forced-colors media query
features.without: In a forced-colours mode the browser's own adjustments apply, without the components' fixes.

features.name: overscroll-behavior: contain
features.without: Scrolling past the end of a list carries on scrolling the page.
